title: Collections Standard — Delinquency, Right to Cure and Charge-Off on Home Purchase Financing Loans
content:
**Collections department standard (Home Purchase Financing)**

**Delinquency.** A loan becomes delinquent when its oldest unpaid installment is the program's delinquency days past due, and returns to active when payments bring it back under that threshold. Days past due are the calendar days by which the handling date is after the due date of the oldest unpaid installment, zero when that date is today or later.

**Credit reporting.** The delinquency is reported to the credit bureaus at the program's credit-reporting days past due.

**Right to cure.** The right-to-cure notice is sent at the program's right-to-cure notice days past due, stating the past-due installments plus fees owed and a cure deadline the program's cure-period days in calendar days after the notice date.

**Charge-off.** A loan is charged off only when its oldest unpaid installment has been past due for the program's charge-off days, counted from the installment due date. The past-due period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the installment due date, and the loan qualifies on the day the count reaches the charge-off days. The due date is read from the company's loan record. On charge-off the remaining principal is written off.

**Collections matters.** Repossession, legal action and settlement of a charged-off balance are handled only by the collections department; the resident desk never schedules, threatens or negotiates them, and such requests go to a human representative.

### Charge-off boundary (hypothetical dates, charge-off days taken as 120)

| Oldest unpaid due date | Date | Day of the count | Qualifies for charge-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | 2026-04-30 | 119 | no |
| 2026-01-01 | 2026-05-01 | 120 | yes — the count has reached 120 |

The count starts on 2026-01-02 as day 1; equality with the charge-off days satisfies the condition.
